findings.title: FAITHFULNESS: emergencyTransfer breaks story-008 HIGH-5's promise of a safe pauseWithdraw exit after a drain - post-drain pauseWithdraw reverts for everyone (carries V1 -> V2)
findings.specText: story-008 (commit d46506a, HIGH-5): "After emergencyTransfer removes all tokens, the contract is now automatically paused, preventing any new stakes or normal withdrawals. Users can safely exit via pauseWithdraw() without claiming rewards, prioritizing principal recovery over rewards in emergency situations."
findings.specSource: git commit d46506a body (HIGH-5 fix) + PhlimboV2.sol L276-279 NatSpec restating the safe-exit promise
findings.intendedBehavior: After an emergency, pauseWithdraw is the user's safe principal-recovery exit: the contract is paused and each user can withdraw their staked phUSD principal.
findings.actualBehavior: emergencyTransfer (L251-263) transfers the ENTIRE phUSD balance to `recipient` and then _pause()s, but never zeroes userInfo[].amount or totalStaked. Post-drain, pauseWithdraw (L280-291) decrements user.amount/totalStaked and then safeTransfer(phUSD) (L288) the contract no longer holds — so every user's pauseWithdraw reverts on the token transfer. The advertised safe-exit recovers nothing once emergencyTransfer has fired.
findings.deviation: Story-008 promises pauseWithdraw is a working post-emergency principal exit; in V2 the emergency drain leaves stale accounting and no balance, so the exit reverts for all users. Identical shape to V1 (Phlimbo.sol L214-261); the V2 rewrite carries the deviation unchanged.
findings.lawBasis: Law 2 (faithfulness). Not a Law-1 escalation on its own: reaching the broken state requires emergencyTransfer, an owner action; the deviation is that the story's stated user-facing guarantee is false, which is a spec-conformance defect, not a standalone exploit path.
findings.ledgerNote: Carries ledger F-01 (fingerprint phlimbo:emergencyTransfer+pauseWithdraw:false-recovery-promise-faithfulness) from src/Phlimbo.sol into src/PhlimboV2.sol; v2Disposition already recorded as CARRIES-INTO-V2.

findings.title: story-020 change #2 (migrator routing): implementation is FAITHFUL; intended design diverts a pre-existing position's rewards to the caller - footgun, not a malicious-owner vector
findings.specText: story-020 change #2: "The migrator can act on behalf of any user ... Tokens and auto-claimed rewards always land in msg.sender (the caller)."
findings.specSource: git commit ac42de6 body (story-020) + PhlimboV2.sol L317-338, L403-432, L479-507 NatSpec
findings.intendedBehavior: stake/withdraw/claim accept an explicit `user`; auth is msg.sender == user || msg.sender == migrator; the caller (msg.sender) always receives withdrawn tokens and auto-claimed rewards. _claimRewards(user, beneficiary=msg.sender) routes accrued rewards to the caller.
findings.actualBehavior: Faithful: claim(user) by the migrator mints/transfers the USER's accrued rewards to the MIGRATOR (L424 -> _claimRewards beneficiary = msg.sender -> L495/L500); withdraw(amount,user) likewise (L373); and stake(amount,user) auto-claims a PRE-EXISTING position's rewards to the migrator (L336-338). Implementation matches the story word-for-word.
findings.deviation: None vs the story text (faithful). The reviewable surface is whether the *intended* routing is safe.
findings.lawBasis: Law-1 override assessed and DECLINED as a security escalation; routed to Law-3 footgun triage instead. Verdict: in the actual migration design (story-021), MigratorV1V2.migrateDeposits stakes into FRESH V2 positions (userInfo[user].amount == 0 at seed time), so the auto-claim branch (L336 `if amount > 0`) never fires during the intended flow and no rewards are diverted. Diversion only bites if (a) a user self-stakes into V2 BEFORE the migrator acts on them (nothing prevents this - stake is permissionless self-service), or (b) the migrator role is later pointed at a populated-position user. Both require an owner having set a migrator AND that migrator calling on an already-staked user. Under a non-malicious owner running the documented lifecycle this does not occur, so it is NOT a Law-1 reward-misappropriation finding and is adequately covered by owner-trust for the happy path. It IS a non-obvious footgun: a competent owner would be surprised that a routine migrator stake/claim on a user who happened to pre-stake silently sends that user's rewards to the migrator wallet rather than the user. Surfaced as a Low operational hazard with safe-config guidance (do not run the migrator against users with pre-existing V2 positions; or settle/migrate before users can self-stake).
findings.safeConfigGuidance: Sequence migration so users cannot self-stake into V2 before migrateDeposits runs (e.g. setMigrator + complete migration before publicizing V2 staking), or treat any non-empty pre-existing position as out-of-scope for migrator action. The migrator MUST be the MigratorV1V2 contract, never an EOA; an EOA migrator on a populated position would pocket that user's rewards (still an owner-config footgun, not a malicious-owner report).

findings.title: story-020 change #3 (hook): a reverting/gas-griefing hook that bricks stake/withdraw/claim is an ACKNOWLEDGED-and-safe story intent, not an unflagged footgun
findings.specText: story-020 change #3 + IPhlimboHook NatSpec: "Hooks fire AFTER all internal state mutations and external token transfers complete, inside PhlimboV2's nonReentrant guard. The owner of PhlimboV2 is trusted to set non-malicious hooks; a reverting hook will revert the outer call."
findings.specSource: git commit ac42de6 body (story-020) + src/interfaces/IPhlimboHook.sol L10-13
findings.intendedBehavior: Optional IPhlimboHook invoked after state+transfers, zero-address-guarded (no default no-op contract), inside nonReentrant. A reverting hook reverts the outer stake/withdraw/claim. Owner is trusted to set a non-malicious hook. pauseWithdraw is deliberately hook-exempt (L277-278) so the emergency exit cannot be bricked by a hook.
findings.actualBehavior: Faithful: hooks fire post-state/post-transfer (L353-355, L398-400, L429-431), zero-guarded, inside nonReentrant; pauseWithdraw invokes no hook. A reverting hook reverts stake/withdraw/claim exactly as documented.
findings.deviation: None. The brick-on-revert behavior is an EXPLICITLY documented and acknowledged property of the story, not a hidden consequence. Setting a reverting hook is an obvious owner misconfiguration (Law 3: obvious misuse is trusted/suppressed), and the design already protects the principal-exit path by exempting pauseWithdraw. No surprise to a competent non-malicious owner.
findings.lawBasis: Law 2 (faithful) + Law 3 (the only break requires an obviously-bad owner-set hook; pauseWithdraw escape hatch is hook-exempt). Not a footgun: consequence is obvious and explicitly stated. Informational only.

findings.title: story-021 (MigratorV1V2): lifecycle is FAITHFULLY implemented, but the strict == balance preconditions are an UNSAFE story intent - a 1-wei third-party donation grief-DoSes settleDebt/migrateDeposits (Law-1 override)
findings.specText: story-021 / MigratorV1V2 L152-153: "Both balance preconditions are strict equalities. Strict == catches operator over-funding mistakes — the recovery is withdrawAll." Implemented at settleDebt L159-163 (usdc.balanceOf == totalUSDC AND phUSD.balanceOf == totalPHUSD_deposited) and migrateDeposits L207-210 (phUSD.balanceOf == totalPHUSD_deposited).
findings.specSource: git commit 1b1a32c body (story-021) + MigratorV1V2.sol L152-153, L159-163, L207-210
findings.intendedBehavior: settleDebt and migrateDeposits gate on EXACT-equality of the contract's USDC/phUSD balances against the seeded totals, deliberately, to catch operator over-funding so the operator notices and recovers via withdrawAll.
findings.actualBehavior: Faithful to the story. But because USDC and phUSD are freely transferable, ANY third party can send 1 wei of USDC (or phUSD) to the migrator at any point, making usdc.balanceOf(address(this)) != totalUSDC (or phUSD balance != totalPHUSD_deposited). Every subsequent settleDebt / migrateDeposits then reverts on the strict == precondition. The migration is bricked until the owner notices and runs withdrawAll, which ABORTS the entire migration (it pulls all funds to the owner and the next settle/migrate reverts on the now-empty balance) - so the owner must re-fund and resume, and the griefer can repeat the 1-wei donation indefinitely, including between withdrawAll and re-funding. Cost to attacker: 1 wei + gas. Impact: griefer-controlled DoS / liveness failure of a one-shot, owner-orchestrated migration of all V1 users.
findings.deviation: The implementation does exactly what story-021 specifies; the STORY INTENT itself is unsafe. Per Law 1 (overrides Law 2), a faithful implementation of an exploitable design is still a finding - flagged as story-unsafe rather than a faithfulness note.
findings.lawBasis: Law 1 override of Law 2. The strict == is intended (Law 2 faithful) but enables a permissionless, repeatable, ~free third-party griefing DoS of the migration lifecycle (Law 1). This is NOT an owner footgun (Law 3) - the trigger is an external attacker, not an owner action; over-funding-detection could be achieved with a `>=` lower-bound check (or by sweeping excess) without exposing an equality that any donor can violate. Severity Medium: no direct theft, but protocol function/availability (the whole migration) is impacted by an external party at trivial cost; the documented recovery (withdrawAll) does not defeat a persistent griefer.
findings.remediation: Replace strict `==` with `>=` lower-bound preconditions (balance must be AT LEAST the seeded total), or snapshot/track the migrator's own deposited float instead of reading live balanceOf, so an unsolicited donation cannot block progress. If over-funding detection is desired, surface it as a non-blocking event/sweep rather than a hard revert gate.
